newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan shuts down reactor after leakage news delay.
newsitem.headline: Japan shuts down reactor after leakage news delay.

text.p: A state-run firm that admitted covering up details of Japan's worst nuclear accident last month was ordered to shut down a separate atomic reactor late on Tuesday after delaying reporting another mishap this week.

Authorities ordered the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) to halt operations at its "Fugen" reactor in western Japan after learning it had waited 30 hours before reporting a radiation leak which occurred on Monday.
"The reactor shut down on Tuesday night," a PNC spokesman said by telephone on Wednesday.
The PNC is already facing possible legal action over its handling of an accident last month at a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant northeast of Tokyo.
"Our report was delayed because of our misjudgment. I am sorry for causing trouble," Norito Takeshita, head of the Fugen plant, told a news conference on Tuesday.
The advanced thermal reactor is located in Tsuruga, Fukui Prefecture.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who last week said revelations of PNC's earlier cover-up made him "speechless", told reporters he was "disgusted" at the newest revelation.
"I saw the date of the accident and the date the PNC reported. It's completely hopeless!" he told reporters.
Fukui prefectural officials said an alarm went off early on Monday after a high level of the radioactive material tritium was detected in a facility at the plant, Japan's only heavy water reactor.

A PNC official said the leak occurred when heavy water leaked from a water purification system not directly related to the reactor itself. He said the radiation leakage was very small and caused no damage to the environment or injuries to workers.
The cause of the leak was a loose bolt, which had now been tightened, he said.

On Tuesday, just before news of the latest accident, officials from the Science and Technology Agency, which oversees Japan's ambitious nuclear power programme, said they would file a complaint with prosecutors or police against the PNC as early as Wednesday.

The complaint, which would initiate legal action against the PNC or its officials, concerns inaccuracies in a report on a March 11 fire and explosion at a nuclear reprocessing plant which exposed 37 workers to low levels of radiation.

The PNC admitted last week that the report was deliberately altered to falsely suggest that plant workers had checked to ensure that the fire had been doused. The fire flared up later, triggering the explosion.

In December 1995, PNC officials admitted they had lied about inspections and tried to suppress videotape footage of a massive coolant leak at an experimental fast-breeder reactor at Monju, not far from the site of Monday's leakage.
